questions.prompt: What is Docker Compose used for?

options.text: Building a single image faster
Defining and running a multi-container application from one YAML file, managed as a unit
Replacing the Docker daemon
Scanning images for vulnerabilities

questions.explanation: Compose describes a multi-container app in compose.yaml and lets you start, stop, and manage all of it with commands like docker compose up and down.

questions.prompt: How do services in a Compose project reach one another?

options.text: By hard-coded IP addresses
By service name over the network Compose creates for the project
Only if every port is published to the host
They cannot communicate

questions.explanation: Compose puts all services on a shared project network with DNS, so a service connects to another by its service name (for example, db).

questions.prompt: Should a modern Compose file include a top-level `version: "3"` key?

options.text: Yes, it is required
No, it is obsolete under the Compose Specification and should be omitted
Only for databases
Only when using build:

questions.explanation: The top-level version key is obsolete under the current Compose Specification. Compose warns if you include it; leave it out.

questions.prompt: The current Compose command is two words: docker ______ up. (one word)
questions.explanation: Compose v2 is a plugin invoked as docker compose (with a space). The old standalone docker-compose (v1) is retired.

questions.prompt: Does depends_on wait until the dependency is ready to accept connections?

options.text: Yes, it always waits for full readiness
No, it only controls start order; readiness needs a healthcheck and a condition
Yes, but only for databases
No, it has no effect at all

questions.explanation: depends_on controls the order services start, not whether a dependency is ready. Waiting for readiness requires a healthcheck plus condition: service_healthy.

questions.prompt: Which statements about a Compose file and its commands are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: A service can build from a Dockerfile or use a prebuilt image
docker compose down removes the app's containers and network
docker compose up --build rebuilds services that have a build section
You must publish every service's port for the app to work

questions.explanation: Services can build or use an image, down tears the app down, and --build forces a rebuild. You only publish the ports you need reachable from the host.
